input: Research ergonomic chair options for back pain

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Budget is the single biggest filter — a $200 budget leads to completely different recommendations than a $1,500 budget, and it determines which brands and models are even worth researching.

The specific type of back pain (lower back, upper back, posture-related, herniated disc, etc.) directly affects which ergonomic features matter most, such as lumbar support depth, seat tilt, or headrest height.
The chair needs to fit the user's body — height, weight, and build determine seat depth, armrest width, and cylinder height requirements, which vary widely across models.
How many hours per day the chair will be used affects how much to invest in quality and which durability or cushioning features matter most.
Whether the user wants a shortlist of options, a comparison table, a single recommendation, or links to buy determines the format and depth of the final output.

Some people prioritise mesh vs. foam, aesthetic style, specific brand trust, or adjustability features — these preferences narrow the field significantly and prevent recommending chairs the user would immediately dislike.
Knowing whether 'done well' means a doctor-recommended chair, the best value-for-money pick, or the most adjustable option changes the evaluation criteria used to rank and select chairs.

gold.taskTitle: Research ergonomic chairs for back pain relief
gold.taskDescription: Find and evaluate ergonomic chair options suited to relieving or preventing back pain.

questions.title: What is your total budget for this chair?
questions.description: Establish a clear price range (e.g., under $300, $300–$700, $700–$1,500, or no limit) to filter options appropriately.

questions.title: Which part of your back causes the most pain?
questions.description: Identify whether the pain is in the lower back, upper back, tailbone, or is posture/disc-related, so the right ergonomic features can be prioritised.

questions.title: What are your height and weight measurements?
questions.description: Collect body dimensions to match seat depth, cylinder height range, and weight capacity to the user's physical build.

questions.title: How many hours a day will you sit in this chair?
questions.description: Determine usage intensity — light use (under 4 hrs) vs. full workday (6–10 hrs) significantly affects how much cushioning, breathability, and build quality matters.

questions.title: Do you prefer mesh, foam padding, or no preference?
questions.description: Capture material and style preferences (mesh for breathability, foam/leather for firmness/aesthetics) to avoid recommending chairs the user would dislike on feel or look.

questions.title: What should the final research output look like?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants a single top recommendation, a shortlist with pros and cons, a comparison table, or purchase links.

questions.title: What matters most — value, adjustability, or expert endorsement?
questions.description: Define the primary success criterion so chairs can be ranked by what the user actually cares about: best price-to-quality ratio, maximum adjustability, or clinical/professional recommendation.
